Decision 3 uses 'Why:' instead of 'Rationale:' as the label. Minor style inconsistency vs. other decisions which use 'Rationale:'. Does not affect readability or content completeness.

Decisions 4, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11 use 'Why:' instead of 'Rationale:' as the label, and most lack an explicit 'Alternatives considered:' field. Decisions 1, 2, and 6 follow the full Decision + Rationale + Alternatives format. The template requires all three fields per decision. Decisions missing 'Alternatives considered:' are: Decision 3 (BCrypt — no alternatives), Decision 4 (says 'No Bucket4j' implicitly but no explicit field), Decision 7 (no alternatives stated), Decision 8 (no alternatives), Decision 9 (no alternatives), Decision 10 (no alternatives), Decision 11 (no alternatives).

Decisions 3, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 are marked [TECHNICAL] or have no References field at all. Per the validation requirement, every decision must reference a user-spec requirement OR be explicitly marked [TECHNICAL]. Decisions 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 contain neither a 'References:' line nor a '[TECHNICAL]' marker. Decision 4 references US-6 and US-5 in References field — correct. Decision 7 has no References or [TECHNICAL] marker. Decision 8 has no References or [TECHNICAL] marker. Decision 9 has no References or [TECHNICAL] marker. Decision 10 explicitly states '[TECHNICAL]' in the Why field inline. Decision 11 explicitly states '[TECHNICAL]' in the Why field inline.

Decision 7 (resend-verification public endpoint) and Decision 8 (CORS for local dev) lack both a 'References:' line and an explicit '[TECHNICAL]' marker as standalone text. The content implies they are technical decisions, but the marker is embedded in prose ('Why: [TECHNICAL]') inconsistently across decisions. Recommend adding explicit '[TECHNICAL]' label or References field to all decisions for consistency.

issues.section: Implementation Tasks — Wave Conflict (Task 5 and Task 6)
issues.finding: Wave 3 contains Task 5 and Task 6 as parallel tasks. Task 5 modifies 'backend/src/main/java/com/botfunnel/auth/AuthController.java' and 'AuthService.java'. Task 6 also modifies the same two files. Parallel execution will create git merge conflicts. One of these tasks must be moved to a later wave, or they must be merged into a single task.
Testing Strategy is present, well-structured, and specifies 'Feature size: L'. Covers unit, integration (Testcontainers), E2E (Playwright), and frontend component tests. No finding.

Acceptance Criteria section is present and comprehensive. One item contains a logic error: '[ ] JobRunr hard-delete job removes users with deletedAt < 30d ago; users with deletedAt < 30d ago remain' — both clauses say the same condition. Should read: 'users with deletedAt < 30d ago remain' vs 'users with deletedAt > 30d ago are removed' (i.e., the second clause should be 'users with deletedAt within 30 days remain'). This is a copy-paste error in the AC wording.

Task 2 description is 3 sentences but covers 3 distinct concerns: User @Document + Repository + Service, SecurityConfig extension, and AppException/ErrorHandler in common package. These are logically separate areas. This is within tech-spec scope (defining what to build, not how), but the task is broad. Given the L-size feature and wave constraints, this is acceptable. No critical finding.

summary: The tech-spec for 02-auth is well-structured and exceptionally detailed for an L-size feature. It passes all structural checks. Two critical wave conflict issues exist: Task 5 (Registration) and Task 6 (Logout/Password Reset) are both in Wave 3 and both modify AuthController.java and AuthService.java — parallel execution will cause merge conflicts. These two tasks must be sequenced (one in Wave 3, one in Wave 4) or merged. Additional minor issues: 7 of 11 decisions lack an explicit 'Alternatives considered:' field; 'Files to read' is missing from tasks 2-6; Task 7 description slightly exceeds the 5-sentence guideline; one AC item has a copy-paste error in the logic condition (both clauses reference same direction). No missing sections, no wrong skills, no time estimates, no AC/TDD anchors in task descriptions. Verdict: WARN — fix the Wave 3 file conflict before execution.
